text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate detected for /v1/generate across eu-west-1 -> fallback policy triggered repeatedly. Alert: router.fallback.loop (sev=2). links: https://monitoring.redwood/alerts/1793456789

sam: acked, oncall here. seeing a spike of 502/503 from several customers. digging into router logs now.

jess: I see repeated route changes in router logs: policyId=policy-smart-route-3 falling back to model-quantized-v1 then to model-small-v0 in quick succession. Looks like capacity signal is flapping.

mike: Dedicated pool for eu-west-1 shows healthy GPUs (util avg 18%) but router metrics show pool.available_instances=0 at times. suspect metric pipeline or exporter misreporting.

natalie: Paging history: autoscale triggered up but router metric read shows 0 capacity so requests routed to fallback region -> increased latency and then fallback to smaller variant -> quality issues. Customer impact: at least 4 tenants reported timeouts/ degraded responses.

sam: Running quick check: `curl -s http://router-metrics/eu-west-1 | jq .pools.dedicated-eu.available_instances` -> returning 0 sometimes. Running again returns 12. Weird.

jess: Paste of router log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T09:02:12Z] policy-eval: pool_capacity=0 -> choose_fallback(region=us-east-1,model=model-small-v0)
[2026-03-15T09:02:13Z] policy-eval: pool_capacity=12 -> route_to(dedicated-eu,model=model-quantized-v1)
[2026-03-15T09:02:14Z] policy-eval: pool_capacity=0 -> choose_fallback(...)
```

mike: That looks like a stale metric from the exporter. infra-bot, any rolling restarts on pool exporters?

infra-bot: No rolling restarts logged in last 24h. Exporter version v2.1.1. No deploy events. Disk pressure alerts in eu-west-1 infra at 08:50Z but resolved.

natalie: Are we sure autoscaler actually provisioned instances? check scheduler events for the dedicated pool.

sam: Scheduler events:
```
2026-03-15T08:59:50Z scale_up request id=scale-827 accepted new_instances=10
2026-03-15T09:00:10Z instance_attach id=inst-231 result=success
2026-03-15T09:01:40Z heartbeat inst-231 alive
```
So instances are up.

jess: So the source is likely the metrics aggregator or the router's cache for pool availability. Router seems to read a cached 0 for a few seconds then updates. But policy evaluation is immediate and causes fallback loops.

mike: Immediate mitigation proposals:
- Disable aggressive fallback policy for eu-west-1 (set min-stable-window=15s)
- Add temporary throttle for cross-region fallbacks
- Force router to use last-known good capacity for 30s

sam: I'll apply policy change #1 now (low risk). If successful we should see fewer fallbacks.

sam: `PUT /config/policies/policy-smart-route-3 {"min_stable_window_s":15}` -> 200 OK

jess: Observability: fallback count decreased from 120/min -> 5/min after change. Latency for affected requests dropping.

natalie: Noted customer impact: tickets 12345, 12352, 12360 show 503s from 08:58-09:08, some retries succeeded after minute 09:03. Will coordinate post-incident outreach.

mike: Root cause hypothesis: intermittent metric loss from exporter leading to transient pool_available=0 signals; router treats 0 as hard failure and triggers fallback immediately with no damping. We need a sticky grace period or use autoscaler lease as authoritative.

emily: I'm taking oncall for next 2 hours. Sam can you do a quick handoff? What remaining mitigations do we want in place?

sam: Handoff notes:
- Policy min_stable_window increased to 15s (reverted when issue is verified fixed)
- Reduced cross-region fallback to rate limit 5/s from this router
- Investigate exporter v2.1.1 metric emission jitter (mike + infra)
- Postmortem owners: jess (routing), mike (metrics), natalie (customer comms)
- Current state: fallback rate back near baseline, dedicated pool healthy, monitoring dash updated

emily: ACK. I'll keep the policy change in place and watch for any regression. If we see capacity=0 again, don't escalate to full page unless customer impact > 5 tenants.

jess: We'll instrument router to treat brief zeros as soft-fail next week (feature ticket created: RNW-4572).

mike: I'll open an infra ticket for exporter stability and add more heartbeat metrics (RNW-INF-232).

natalie: I'll start customer outreach draft and coordinate with support for affected tenants.

sam: Thanks team. Marking this as mitigated in the incident tracker. Leaving detailed logs in the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/1793456789. Emily, please update if anything new pops up during your watch.

emily: Will do. Beginning 2hr watch. Handing off channel to emily. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to sev=3 (mitigated). Auto-close timer set for 24h unless updated.
